newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends mixed in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trading on Thursday, with the short-term market trend remaining unclear, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 3,235 yuan ($389) per tonne, rising 37 yuan. It opened at 3,194 and hit a low of 3,190.
March fell 10 to 3,230, May was unchanged at 3,332, July rose nine to 3,380, September rose seven to 3,389 and November was unchanged at 3,399.
Combined volume fell to 10,000 tonnes from 11,200.
Traders said investors did not want to build positions because of uncertainties over the short-term market trend.
"A wait-and-see attitude dominated today's trading," one trader said. "Soybeans are likely to stay around the 3,200-yuan level in the next few days," he added.
